data.title: Las Vegas looks to boost traffic with rare resort-wide sale
data.description:
Las Vegas is on the tail end of a rare citywide five-day sale that ran this week. The Vegas 5-Day sale sees resorts cut prices on rooms, dining, entertainment, and attractions as the industry looks to boost tourism amid an uneven recovery period.

The Vegas 5-Day Sale, running from September 22 through September 26, features more than 180 offers across the Strip, downtown, and surrounding resort corridors. Participating properties are advertising discounts of up to 60% on hotel stays, while other promotions include restaurant credits, show tickets, spa services, attractions, and multi-night packages.

The event is unusual because the offers are coordinated across the destination and compressed into a five-day booking window. The Las Vegas Convention and Visitors Authority launched the first such citywide sale in September 2025, calling it the "Fabulous 5-Day Sale." This year’s event is only its second iteration and expanded to more than 180 deals.

The gambling and entertainment city drew about 38.5M visitors in 2025, a 7.5% decline from the prior year and roughly 3.1M fewer people than in 2024. However, through July this year, visitation had edged 0.5% higher year over year, with July alone up 2.7%, suggesting a modest rebound is gearing up. International travel remains a concern as Canadian visitation, historically the city’s largest international source, remains about 30% below 2019 levels.

Sector watch: Caesars Entertainment (CZR), MGM Resorts (MGM), Boyd Gaming (BYD), Wynn Resorts (WYNN), Full House Resorts (FLL), Bally's Corporation (BALY), VICI Properties (VICI), Sportradar (SRAD), Genius Sports (GENI), Gaming & Leisure Properties (GLPI), and Red Rock Resorts (RRR).

data.title: SK hynix US unit considering IPO at $150B valuation: report
data.description:
SK hynix's (SKHY) U.S. subsidiary, Solidigm, is considering an initial public offering that would value the unit at $150B, Reuters reported.

The unit held meetings with investment banks this week to discuss their pitches, the news outlet added, citing multiple people familiar with the matter. If the unit does go public, it could raise as much as $15B in the offering, three people familiar with the matter said. The size of the deal and timing have not yet been determined, the people added.

SK hynix did not immediately respond to a request for comment from Seeking Alpha.

Solidigm is SK hynix's NAND flash memory and solid-state drive unit and is partially comprised of a 2020 acquisition that saw SK hynix purchase Intel's (INTC) NAND unit.

SK hynix said earlier this month that no determination had been made about raising capital for Solidigm.

“The company hereby clarifies that, while the company's overseas subsidiary under the brand name 'Solidigm' is reviewing various measures to strengthen its competitiveness, no matters have been determined as of the date hereof,” SK hynix said in a statement. “The company will make a further disclosure either when specific details are confirmed or within three months of the date of this report.”

The prolific South Korean memory maker sold 177.9M American Depository Receipt shares priced at $149 each in July, raising $26.5B. As such, SK hynix became the the largest initial public offering ever by a foreign company in the U.S., surpassing Alibaba (BABA) in 2014.

data.title: Scholar Rock added to Wedbush's Best Ideas List
data.description:
• Outperform-rated Scholar Rock Holding Corp. (SRRK) has been added to Wedbush's Best Ideas List as it is "uniquely positioned to deliver a durable, de-risked commercial ramp in the neuromuscular space."
  • The firm has a $70 price target (44% upside based on Sept. 24 close).
  • Analyst David Nierengarten said that the company is being helped by Isembyld's (apitegromab) first-in-class launch for spinal muscular atrophy and its myostatin pipeline.
  • He noted that a recent pullback in shares, likely due to a US FDA post-marketing safety commitment for Isembyld and lower-than-expected pricing, provides an attractive entry point. 
  • Nierengarten sees Isembyld US revenue of ~$5M this year, rising to $140M in 2027, $349M in 2028, and $634M in 2029. Worldwide revenue could surpass $2B by 2031.
  • He added that studies examining Isembyld in SMA patients under the age of two years old and for facioscapulohumeral muscular dystrophy could provide additional upside.

data.title: High beta leads S&P 500 factors in rising-yield environment: S&P Global
data.description:
S&P Global data show that high-beta and value-oriented stocks have historically been the most sensitive S&P 500 factors to rising Treasury yields, while low-volatility and dividend-focused strategies have tended to perform relatively worse.

The analysis measures S&P 500 factor performance for every 100-basis-point move in the U.S. 10-year Treasury yield, based on data from July 7, 1995, through Sept. 23, 2026.

High Beta recorded the strongest relative performance, at 4.9% for each 100-bp rise in the 10-year yield, followed by Pure Value at 2.3% and GARP at 1.3%.

Other factors also posted positive relative performance when yields increased, according to S&P Global. Pure Growth returned 1.0% relative to the S&P 500 per 100-bp increase in the 10-year yield, while Buyback and Equal Weighted each registered 0.8%.

The data highlight a notable historical distinction between more economically sensitive or value-oriented exposures and several traditionally defensive factor strategies when Treasury yields move higher.

On the other side of the spectrum, Low Volatility had the most negative relationship with rising yields, with relative performance of -2.7% per 100-bp increase in the 10-year Treasury yield. Dividend Aristocrats followed at -1.2%, while Momentum posted -0.8% and Quality -0.5%.

The growth factor also showed negative relative performance of 0.4% for each 100-bp increase in yields. The historical relationship suggests that rising rates have not affected all factor strategies in the same way, with defensive and income-oriented exposures showing greater sensitivity in the data.

The findings come as Treasury yields remain an important driver of U.S. equity-market performance. The 10-year Treasury yield has recently traded around the 5% level, with higher yields putting pressure on equity valuations by raising the discount rate applied to future corporate cash flows.

Recent market data have also shown periods when rising yields weighed on stocks, although strong earnings expectations and AI-related growth have helped support equities.  S&P Global's historical factor analysis therefore provides a framework for assessing how different parts of the S&P 500 have responded to changes in the rate environment over the long term.

data.title: Ford F-150 production halted at a Detroit plant
data.description:
Ford Motor Company (F) halted production of its F-150 pickup truck at a plant near Detroit, according to a memo spotted by Reuters. All shifts for production crews at Dearborn Truck Plant were canceled through September 29, according to the memo.

Sources indicate production of the F-150 truck at other plants was also impacted by the same unspecified issue.

Last year, fires at supplier Novelis’s New York aluminum plant disrupted material for Ford's (F) F-150 and other F-Series trucks. The plant restarted its hot mill in June 2026, and Ford (F) has since increased production, although dealer inventory remained below its target in early September. Looking further back, a semiconductor shortage caused repeated pauses or reduced schedules for F-150 production, including at Dearborn in 2021 and Kansas City in 2022.

Shares of Ford (F) were up 1.2% in Friday afternoon trading.

data.title: Yields bite, but 'smart money' still gorging on AI - Vanda
data.description:
"Equity (SPY) (QQQ) positioning has de-risked meaningfully this week as higher yields (US2Y) (US10Y) (US30Y) start to bite, but the composition is more constructive than the headline suggests," Vanda Research said in a Friday note.

Institutional investors are demonstrating notable resilience amid macroeconomic volatility stemming from a steep bond-market rout. Specifically, one-month institutional options flows stand at +$18.4B, which is roughly three times the typical flow volume seen during September, Vanda noted.

More crucially, these flows have reversed course and trended upward over the past five sessions, providing a reasonably constructive signal for risk appetite beneath the broader market de-risking.

 

 

Rather than retreating entirely, institutional capital is actively being deployed into select artificial intelligence (AIQ) (AIEQ) equities. Per Vanda's options flow data, Meta Platforms (META) is the most-bought mega-cap stock by institutions this week and is on track for its third-biggest week of institutional call buying in two years.

Over a four-session span, institutions added $603M of net call exposure to Meta (META). This aggressive positioning is second only to Micron Technology (MU) across the entire market, while Meta's gross call turnover has surged 243% above last week's levels.

Ultimately, Vanda said, the data indicate that macro uncertainty is not stopping risk-taking; it is simply forcing investors to be far more selective.

data.title: Midday Need to Know: Trump’s AI meeting, PayPal takeover speculation & more
data.description:
U.S. equities pushed higher Friday as yields eased and further development around the reopening of the Strait of Hormuz continued.

The blue-chip Dow (DJI) was last +0.9%, the benchmark S&P 500 (SP500) was last +0.5%, and the tech-focused Nasdaq Composite (COMP:IND) was last +0.6%.

Now, here are 4 news stories that broke in the morning to watch out for:

Trump and Speaker Johnson to meet with top tech CEOs on AI safety: President Donald Trump and House Speaker Mike Johnson  plan to host leading technology executives at the White House on Tuesday, Sept. 29, for discussions on artificial intelligence safety and potential government oversight. The meeting follows rising concerns from experts about AI's destructive potential without proper guardrails, though Trump has dismissed such warnings as a "hoax" while emphasizing the need for U.S. firms to outpace China in the AI race. 

Natural gas prices fall 5.5% as pipeline leak impact proves brief: U.S. front-month Nymex natural gas futures  dropped 5.5% to $3.115/MMBtu on Friday, reversing much of Thursday's 9% surge that followed a force majeure on TC Energy's Mountaineer Xpress pipeline in West Virginia. The leak had cut firm transportation service by 1.8 Bcf/day, affecting roughly 1.5% of total U.S. Lower-48 gas supply. Analysts at Ritterbusch & Associates noted the outage appears likely to be brief, adding that Thursday's sharp price response was exacerbated by heavy speculative short positioning built up during the summer's storage cushion.

PayPal ticks up amid rumors of West Coast tech takeover interest: PayPal  (PYPL)  shares  rose 1.2% on renewed acquisition speculation after traders cited a Betaville report indicating an unnamed West Coast technology company may be evaluating an all-stock takeover of the fintech firm. The PayPal board is said to prefer an all-cash deal. The speculation follows the collapse of talks between a Stripe and Advent consortium, which had considered offering as much as $68 per share in cash but abandoned the pursuit last month after negotiations stalled over a $2 billion breakup fee.

Elevated short interest keeps squeeze risk high for crypto-linked stocks: Short-squeeze risk remains  elevated across major bitcoin-linked equities, according to S3 Partners Director of Research Leon Gross. Strategy, Strive, and Coinbase each show return correlations above 0.70 with bitcoin, while short interest hovers near 10-13% of float for Strategy and Coinbase. Bitcoin has rallied more than 50% from its lows this year but remains down year to date. S3 noted that Strive, with its smaller market capitalization of roughly $3 billion, experienced a squeeze in August when shares rose sharply alongside declining short interest, while larger names like Strategy ($65 billion market cap) and Coinbase ($53 billion) remain too large for short covering alone to drive similar moves.

data.title: Stocks climb as Hormuz talks turn technical and oil slides
data.description:
U.S. equity averages extended their advance Friday afternoon as crude prices retreated on reports that Washington and Tehran had shifted their discussions from opening contacts to a more technical stage.

Oil (CL1:COM) fell about 3% to roughly $91.70 a barrel, while Brent (CO1:COM) slipped about 4% to near $103.33, as traders priced in a possible path toward restoring commercial traffic through the Strait of Hormuz. 

Al Jazeera’s Tehran bureau chief, Nourddine Dgheir, said sources in the Iranian capital described the tone as increasingly constructive. The Qatari-owned network reported that technical specialists had joined the New York talks after an initial session involving U.S. envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner. Qatar has mediated between the two governments for months. 

Moreover, U.S. officials did not immediately confirm that the negotiations had moved to the technical level. Even so, the combination of lower energy prices and the prospect of a sequenced reopening of the waterway supported another bid higher in the major stock indexes as investors weighed whether diplomacy could ease a key supply risk.

data.title: Trump seeks to produce more generic drugs in the US
data.description:
The Trump administration is asking for input from drugmakers on how to manufacture 86 essential generic medications in the US that are now mostly produced abroad.

The Office of Management and Budget will solicit proposals on moving the production of these medicines within 18 months, according to a notice in the Federal Register posted Friday.

"This RFI is seeks information both to optimize use of existing domestic or near shore capacity and to better understand ongoing or planned actions to create new domestic or near shore capacity for essential generic pharmaceuticals on the ASPR 86 list," the documents states.

The 86 essential medicines were determined by the HHS' Office of the Assistant Secretary for Preparedness and Response (“ASPR”), which was last updated in 2022.  

Drugs on the list include the analgesic opioid hydromorphone, the anticoagulant heparin, the cardiovascular treatment metoprolol, the antibiotic vancomycin, the sedative lorazepam, and the steroid methylprednisone. 

In August 2025, Trump signed an executive order to increase the amount of active pharmaceutical ingredients—the raw materials used to make medicines—stockpiled in the US. HHS was also asked to create a list of around 26 critical drugs "vital to national health and security" and to update the ASPR essential medicines list.

data.title: Wall Street rises as yields slip and U.S.-Iran relations remain in focus
data.description:
U.S. equities pushed higher Friday as yields eased and further development around the reopening of the Strait of Hormuz continued.

The blue-chip Dow (DJI) was last +0.9%, the benchmark S&P 500 (SP500) was last +0.5%, and the tech-focused Nasdaq Composite (COMP:IND) was last +0.6%. 

On a sector-by-sector stance, seven of the 11 segments shifted higher, with info tech leading the charge. At the other end of the spectrum, energy suffered the most. 

U.S. and Iranian talks advanced from initial contacts into a more detailed technical phase on reopening the Strait of Hormuz, with sources in Tehran describing a more constructive atmosphere, Al Jazeera’s Tehran bureau chief Nourddine Dgheir reported.

On the economic calendar, durable goods orders growth stalled in August, better than the decline expected. Moreover, consumer sentiment for September was revised to 48.1 from the initial print of 47.8 and 51.7 in August.

The U.S. 2-year Treasury yield (US2Y) slipped 7 basis points to 4.85%, the U.S. 10-year Treasury yield (US10Y) moved down by 4 basis points to 5.17%, and the U.S. 30-year Treasury yield (US30Y) ticked lower by 1 basis point to 5.49%. 

“Interest rates are rising at a fast pace, which means the cost of money is rising at a fast pace. While stocks were initially applauding the Fed's attention to inflation and action on rates with the September hike, they're now waking up to the fact that the entire yield curve is going up. This is a negative for bonds and stocks,” Richard Reyle of Questar Capital Partners stated.

As for stocks that were on the move, shares of Datadog (DDOG) advanced +6.1%, while shares of Palo Alto Networks (PANW) fell -2.8%.
